Subordinate Judge, 5th Court and Artha Rin Adalat. Khulna and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mr. Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman, J. In this Rule the judgment and order dated 07-05-2000 passed exparte in Misc. Case No. 23 of 1997 by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna, has been challenged being passed without jurisdiction and without lawful authority. 

 2. The writ petitioner asserted that respondent Bangladesh Shilpa Bank for realization of its due money filed Misc. Case No. 23 of 1997 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna under Article 33(1) of the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank Order, 1972, on payment of the Court fee of Tk. 5/- only in the form an application and the Artha Rin Adalat on misconception of law entertained the case illegally and passed the impugned judgment and order having had no jurisdiction under Section-33(1) of the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank Order, 1972 i.e. P.O. 129 of 1972. The respondent Bangladesh Shilpa Bank contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition stating that the writ petitioner cannot raise the question of jurisdiction now as he had opportunity to raise the said question of jurisdiction before the Trial Court and that there is no denial that the claim of the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank is lawful and the petitioner enjoyed loan from the respondent Bank and that the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank Order, 1972 is a special statute and the proceeding under the said statute shall proceed independently and shall prevail over the ordinary law and accordingly the Artha Rin Adalat has rightly decreed the case giving emphasis on the special law and the impugned judgment and order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot be called in question in any Court of law and therefore the Rule is liable to be dis-charged. 

 3. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate, appearing for the writ petitioner, submitted that the impugned judgment and order passed exparte in the Misc. Case by the Artha Rin Adalat is without jurisdiction in as much as the respondent Bank has filed the case under the provisions of Article 33 of P.O. 129 of 1972 on payment of Court Fee of Tk. 5/- and that Article 33(1) of P.O. 129 of 1972 authorises filing an application under the said Article only in the Court of the District Judge and that it has already been settled by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh that the Statutory bodies having special forum for realization of its due money may also avail the ordinary forum but on payment of Advolerum Court Fees. The Artha Rin Adalat acted illegally in entertaining the case filed by the respondent Shilpa Bank under Article 33 of P.O. 129 of 1972 and in support of his contention the learned Advocate placed before us the decision in the case of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation Vs. Jahanara Alder reported in 49 DLR (AD) 80 wherein the Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation filed an application under Article 27 of P.O. 7 of 1973 House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 in the Artha Rin Adalat for realization of its due money in the loan account of the defendant on payment of Special Court fee fixed for such filing of application under said P.O. 7/73 and their Lordships have observed that "a financial institution may institute a suit in connection with realisation of its loan in the Artha Rin Adalat under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and by reason of the proviso in Section-5(1), the special provision or procedure for realisation of loan provided in the law by which the financial institution is established will not be affected. The option is with the financial institution either to bring a suit under Section-5(1) of the Act or to take recourse to special procedure provided in the relevant law" and therefore an application filed in the Artha Rin Adalat adopting the procedure of the Special Law i.e. P.O. 7/73 cannot be entertained, and if entertained the same is without jurisdiction, as in the instant case. 

 4. Mr. Md. Muzibur Rahman Miah, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Bank submitted that the writ petition as filed is not in form and is not maintainable in as much as there being an appellate forum, the petitioner without exhausting the said forum is not entitled to seek any relief under the Writ Jurisdiction. The learned Advocate further submitted that there being no objection raised against the jurisdiction of the Artha Rin Adalat in which the case was filed by the respondent Bank, the judgment and order passed is not illegal and the writ petitioner now cannot raise any objection there against. The learned Advocate further submitted that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain has been promulgated for realization of loan money in a summary manner and there is no bar for filing any case in the Artha Rin Adalat by the respondent Bank and therefore the Rule is liable to be dis-charged with cost. 

 5. We have perused the writ petition and the affidavit-in-opposition. We have considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates of the respective par-ties. We have perused the decision placed before us by the learned Advocate for the petitioner mentioned herein above. It is now a settled law that outstanding loan money can be realised either through the special law or through the ordinary law and if financial institution like the respondent Bangladesh Shilpa Bank wants to realise its outstanding loan money through Artha Rin Adalat, then it must pay Advolerum Court fee and file a plaint for a regular suit but in the instant case the respondent has filed an application not under the normal law but under the special law i.e. under the provisions of Article 33 of P.O. 129 of 1972 and on payment of Court fee Tk. 5/- only. The Section 33 of P.O. 129 of 1972 provides for entertainment of such application only by the District Judge, who is given the exclusive jurisdiction to deal with such application for realization of respondent's due money. The Artha Rin Adalat has no jurisdiction to entertain an application under Section-33 of P.O. 129 of 1972 in view of the decision in the case of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation Vs. Jehanara Akter reported in 49 DLR (AD) 80 and accordingly the Artha Rin Adalat has acted illegally and without jurisdiction in entertaining the Misc. Case and accordingly the impugned judgment and order passed in Misc. Case No. 23 of 1997 vide judgment and order dated 07-05-2000 by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot be maintained being without jurisdiction. 

 6. Accordingly the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order dated 07-05-2000 passed in Misc. Case No. 23 of 1997 by the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna is declared to be made without any lawful authority and of no legal effect.
